newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed, broker takes loss.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed, broker takes loss.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in active trading that saw one local broker scramble for shares in Banco de Colombia, and book a heavy loss, to meet a commitment it made by mistake last month, brokers said.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 0.30 percent to close at 13,553.62 on volume of 958.9 million pesos while Bogota's IBB index slipped 0.08 percent to end at 871.63.
Volume in Bogota was a larger-than-average 2.2 billion pesos, but brokers said nearly 1.3 billion of the total involved Banco de Colombia, which closed unchanged at 442 pesos per share.

Heavy trading in the bank's stock stemmed from buying by local brokerage firm Correval, which was seeking to cover obligations it made last month. A computer operator at the firm allegedly botched a sell order in mid-October, offering to sell three million Banco de Colombia shares instead of 3,000, brokers said.

At least 1.5 million shares were snapped up immediately by a rival brokerage on behalf of a foreign investment fund, and Correval had no choice but to go out and buy the shares at a loss, brokers said.
Spokesmen at Correval could not be reached for imemdiate comment on the computer error, which brokers said had cost it the equivalent of about $35,000.
Gainers in Bogota included brewer Bavaria S.A., the crown jewel of the Santo Domingo conglomerate. Brokers said it rose 0.41 percent on foreign fund buying, closing at 4,080 pesos per share.

Losers included cigarette maker Coltabaco, which ended down 1.63 percent at 3,000 pesos per share, and Banco Ganadero, whose preferential shares fell 5.47 percent to end at the day at 190 a share. Brokers attributed both declines to profit-taking.
